name: diagnose-errors
conclusion_quantitative: diagnose-errors (Escalate) specifies 1 of 5 categories: 4 approval gates; none for autonomy limits, clarification rules, validation rules, escalation rules. Strongest: approval gates.
conclusion_qualitative: diagnose-errors fetches production errors from Sentry and Better Stack, classifies them as mundane (with silencing recommendations) or genuine, and investigates the genuine ones. Its control rules are all approval gates: the user chooses which errors to investigate and approves any fix. It sets no autonomy limits, clarification rules, checks on its own work or rules for escalating failures.

autonomy_limits.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never forbids or restricts any action of the agent on files, commands, tools or other systems, and never tells it to go ahead without asking.

clarification_rules.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to ask the user for missing or unclear information, or to avoid guessing.

approval_gates.conclusion_quantitative: 4 approval gates (3 mandatory, 1 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list.
approval_gates.conclusion_qualitative: There are 4 rules, 3 strict and 1 counted as a suggestion (it contains "should"), none tied to a situation, evenly split between running text and bullet points. After triage the agent stops, presents its findings and waits for the user to confirm which genuine errors to investigate before starting a worktree, and proposes fixes without implementing them unless the user approves.

statements.quote: **STOP HERE and present findings to the user before proceeding.**
Wait for user confirmation on which genuine errors to investigate.
Propose a fix (but do not implement without user approval)
The user should confirm which genuine errors to investigate before you start a worktree

validation.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent to check its own work, such as running tests, or says when the work counts as done.

escalation.conclusion_qualitative: The skill never tells the agent what to do when something goes wrong, such as stopping or reporting an error to the user.
